text:
sasha: quick heads-up — between 12:10–12:20 UTC eu-west had sustained GPU queue depth above 90% and we started seeing a lot of spillover into us-east.
mike: saw that too. was that auto-spillover or our emergency fanout? the logs look like cross-region steer kicked in.
tara: auto-spillover. policy was 'region-preference:eu then spill:us' but priority lanes should have kept premium customers local. looks like lane admission dropped.
oliver: timeline: capacity alarms -> autoscaler tried to add nodes, provisioning lagged -> admission controller started soft-rejects -> spillover to us-east. infra-oncall alerted.
deploy-bot: deploy finished: routing/0.9.3 rolled at 12:05 UTC
sasha: key question: why did premium lane admission fall through? admission controller metrics show token bucket exhaustion for p99 latency.
mike: token bucket exhaustion expected during long tails. but we should have had reserve tokens for premium lanes. config snippet:
```yaml
admission:
  default_qps: 200
  premium_reserve: 0.2 # 20% of capacity
  soft_admit: true
  fallback_rules:
    - condition: region_saturation
      action: spill_to: [us-east, ap-south] 
```
tara: our telemetry shows premium_reserve config was present, but scaler had already moved GPUs to maintenance due to a driver bug, reducing effective capacity. ops ticket created.
oliver: driver bug? which nodes? any correlation with the 11:50 maintenance batch?
infra-oncall: yes — node-pool-g4-3 had a rolling kernel update that hit 10% of the pool; we mis-tagged health checks so they were drained slower.
sasha: ok that explains reduced effective capacity. still want routing to degrade gracefully — we shouldn't drop to soft-reject for premium users before trying model-fallback to smaller quantized variants.
mike: agreed. propose change: routing priority chain = [local-same-model, local-quantized, cross-region-same-model, cross-region-quantized, degrade-low-priority]. Add hysteresis window to avoid flapping.
tara: +1. add cost threshold though — cross-region quantized for heavy throughput can be expensive. maybe prefer local quantized over cross-region same-model if inter-region latency > 60ms.
oliver: suggest this decision tree pseudocode for router:
```python
if local_capacity.available(premium):
  route(local, model.v) 
elif local_capacity.available(quantized):
  route(local, model.v.quant)
elif cross_region_latency < 60ms and cross_capacity.available():
  route(cross_region, model.v)
elif cross_capacity.quant_available:
  route(cross_region, model.v.quant)
else:
  soft_reject or queue with TTL
```
infra-oncall: also add admission metrics: reserve_utilization, quantized_fallback_count, cross_region_egress_cost_estimate — want them visible in console.
sasha: good list. we also need a quick short-term mitigation: bump premium_reserve to 30% when pool-drain events active, and failover to on-demand warm pool rather than immediate cross-region.
mike: short-term patch deployed to staging. will test spike with loadgen.
tara: loadgen test plan: 2k concurrent premium requests with a 2s-model baseline, simulate 15% node drain, confirm fallback path and billing estimate logs.
oliver: one more edge: stateful KV caches — when we fallback to quantized or cross-region, KV cache misses spike and can increase latency. router should prefer quantized local with cached prefix if cache_hit_ratio > 0.6.
sasha: noted. action items:
- mike: run staging loadgen + validate fallback paths (ETA 2h)
- infra-oncall: improve node drain tagging and health-check timing (ETA 4h)
- tara: add metrics panels for reserve_utilization, quantized_fallback_count, cross_region_cost_est (ETA 6h)
- oliver: draft router decision tree + unit tests (ETA end of day)

mike: started loadgen now — I'll post results in this thread. :rocket:
infra-oncall: filing ops-#4127 for maintenance tagging fix.
sasha: thanks team — this one felt like a small cascade: maintenance -> effective capacity drop -> reserve not honored -> immediate spill -> premium users affected. let's keep postmortem short and link to runbooks.
deploy-bot: incident created: INC-2026-eu-west-spillover (linked)
mike: loadgen results: with premium_reserve bumped to 30% we preserve local routing for 92% of requests during simulated drain. quantized fallback used for remaining 8%.
tara: good numbers. can we add a graceful TTL queue for small waits before cross-region to save egress cost?
oliver: TTL queue ok but need to bound memory. implement per-user token expiry and max-wait 500ms.
sasha: sounds good. closing loop: merge routing change PR with decision tree + metrics, infra change for health-check, and an emergency knob in console to raise reserve. I'll re-open if anything else shows up.
mike: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/842
sasha: :thumbsup:
